The supplied base-to-target diff was inspected; it replaces the vanilla frontend with React/Vite and includes the round-1 authentication-race repair.

The committed handoff records 174 backend tests, 88 frontend tests, Python compilation, governance validation, TypeScript compilation, Vite build, and a manual browser walkthrough against the candidate tree.

Independent backend-test execution ran 174 tests but failed with 68 errors because the read-only review sandbox denied loopback socket binding; this is an environment limitation rather than evidence of product-test failures.

The checkout was clean before checks. Test execution did not produce a reported tracked-file change.

evidence: Expected: moving to sample mode or signing out while device-code authentication is in flight must leave both the UI and backend session unauthenticated, so tenant data and tokens do not remain accessible after the abandoned attempt.

Observed: pollOnce drops a stale successful response at line 142, but that response means the server-side /api/auth/poll operation has already completed successfully and installed the authenticated session. The client performs no compensating logout.
viewSampleData only increments the client cancellation/generation tokens and fetches sample data; exitSample only changes client state. Neither calls authLogout.

Consequently, if an in-flight poll succeeds after viewSampleData, the dashboard remains in sample mode as intended, but the backend can retain the live delegated token. Exiting sample then displays signed-out state while /api/policies and /api/analysis can remain authenticated.
The new regression test asserts only that the UI stays in sample mode and does not immediately fetch /api/policies; it does not verify server-session cleanup.
findings.remediation: Add server-aware cancellation/session cleanup for abandoned device-code attempts, with ordering that cannot log out a newer successful authentication attempt. A stale successful poll must not leave credentials installed server-side. Also ensure exiting sample mode cannot present a signed-out UI over an authenticated backend session.
findings.title: Cancelled device-code success can leave a hidden authenticated backend session
findings.verification: Use a deferred integration test where /api/auth/poll succeeds after sample mode is selected. Verify the stale result does not change UI mode, the server no longer retains the token/session, and subsequent /api/policies and /api/analysis requests return unauthenticated. Add equivalent coverage for sign-out and for overlap with a newer authentication attempt.

limitations: The checkout is shallow/grafted: the round-0 commit object 4cb61161be32b43506bb0e2c1b6921635561054d and target parent identity were unavailable locally, so the claimed round-0-to-round-1 delta could not be independently reconstructed. The launcher-supplied base-to-target diff and exact target tree were available.

Backend tests could not complete in this sandbox because all server integration cases requiring loopback socket binding raised PermissionError. Repository-recorded successful output exists, but independent execution failed.
Frontend dependencies are absent, so TypeScript compilation, Vite build, and Vitest were not independently rerun. Installing dependencies is unavailable and would require separate approval.
The manual browser walkthrough has no retained recording and cannot be independently verified from the committed artifact.
No live-tenant authentication or Microsoft Graph access was attempted; those are protected actions and remain deferred.
review.summary: BLOCKED. The round-1 client token prevents stale device-code responses from overwriting React state, but a stale successful poll can still install and retain authentication on the server, leaving a signed-out/sample UI over a live backend session. Independent verification was also incomplete because the sandbox denied loopback binding and frontend dependencies were absent.
